Coinbase Commerce requires users to:

- Provides a familiar checkout flow

Cons:
- Stripe account verification is required

- Payments by credit card
- OAuth authentication
- Converting fiat → crypto

Pros:
- Benefits from trust in the Coinbase brand
- Built-in fiat → crypto conversion

Cons:
- A Coinbase account is required
- The user must purchase crypto first

Services providing genuine fiat → crypto include:
- MoonPay - Credit card → crypto widget

- Wyre - Fiat gateway (being sunset)

- Provides global coverage

In the current design—swapping the full msg.value into USDC and refunding any surplus in USDC—the contract has no route for returning ETH.

Why a contract update is needed
Currently, mintWithETH:
- Wraps the entirety of msg.value into WETH
- Swaps all of the WETH for USDC
- Returns the difference in USDC when usdcReceived > 15 USDC

For refunds to be issued in ETH, the contract cannot swap the entire amount.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Best-practice option for a clean and safe UX
Modify mintWithETH to call Uniswap V3 exactOutputSingle:
- Set the output target to exactly 15\_000\_000 USDC
- Use amountInMaximum = msg.value WETH
- Allow the router to consume only the amount required
- Have the contract unwrap the remaining WETH and return ETH to the payer
- Revert when 15 USDC cannot be obtained within msg.value
- This is the standard approach for guaranteeing the exact USDC mint price while refunding the balance in ETH.

Recommendation
- To avoid any surprises for users, add exactOutputSingle with an ETH refund; this requires a redeploy.
- To maintain stability for now, leave the existing behavior in place and add a brief UI message such as: “Excess is refunded in USDC.” This is the lowest-risk option.
